extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, researchers and fact-checkers interested in misinformation and fake news websites
extracted.subtask_description: Identify, list and annotate websites that publish misinformation, parody presented as fact, cloned/spoofed outlets, or otherwise act as conduits of disinformation; entries note why each domain is flagged (e.g., sharing infrastructure, plagiarism, spoofing, fact-checker debunks, malware).

rubrics_metrics.name: Shares the same IP address or ad network ID
rubrics_metrics.description: Shares the same IP address or ad network ID as departed.co.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to link multiple domains as part of the same network; examples in text include many 'usdeplorables...' domains flagged because they 'Shares the same IP address or ad network ID as departed.co.' (source notes [439]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spoofing a mainstream outlet
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domains that intentionally imitate established news brands (e.g., deceptive domains like 'usfoxnews.com' or 'World-BBC-News.com') to trick readers into believing they are legitimate outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part of a network registered for profit motives
rubrics_metrics.description: Part of network of fake news sites registered in Georgia for profit motives during the 2016 US Presidential Elections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites sharing registration patterns, ownership and coordinated purpose (profit-driven hyperpartisan networks) are flagged as part of systemic misinformation operations (example cited with source [413]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copied from parody/satire sites
rubrics_metrics.description: Copied story from The Postillon, a parody/satire site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites that republish satire/parody content as factual news are flagged (multiple examples: ILoveNativeAmericans.us, NativeAmericans.news, WeLoveNative.com copied from The Postillon; sources: PolitiFact/FactCheck).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism / stolen content
rubrics_metrics.description: Per PolitiFact / news reporting: sites plagiarize or steal articles (e.g., 'A Marketing Site Deleted Over 7,000 Articles After It Was Caught Stealing Fact-Checks And Plagiarizing').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicators include wholesale copying of other outlets' reporting or fact-checks; such behavior has been used to obtain ad revenue and can be evidence a site is not a legitimate news source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fabricated quotes or invented content
rubrics_metrics.description: Copied article from satire/parody site Politicops.com and fabricated quotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites that not only republish but add fabricated quotations or invented details are specifically flagged by fact-checkers (example cited in entry for 'US Political News (USPOLN)').

rubrics_metrics.name: History of publishing demonstrably false claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Published many false claims, including that Donald Trump was endorsed by Pope Francis in 2016.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A track record of false, debunked stories (documented by fact-checkers) is used to classify a site as unreliable or 'fake news' (see 'endingthefed.com' example and related citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accused of participation in foreign propaganda campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Accused by the Foreign Policy Research Institute of being part of a propaganda campaign by Russia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent research or credible reports alleging coordination with state-backed influence operations are used as evidence when classifying domains (example: Ending the Fed / Expunere connection to alleged Russian campaigns).

rubrics_metrics.name: Possibly distributes malware
rubrics_metrics.description: Same owner as CountyNewsroom.info. Possibly spreads malware.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security risk indicators (malware distribution) in addition to misleading content are noted as reasons to distrust or block domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagged/debunked by reputable fact-checkers
rubrics_metrics.description: Per FactCheck.org / PolitiFact / Lead Stories — domains and individual stories have been debunked or documented by established fact-checking organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations to fact-checker reports (PolitiFact, FactCheck.org, Lead Stories, AP, Snopes, etc.) are used as authoritative evidence to mark domains as spreading falsehoods or satire misrepresented as news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain churn and rapid replacement behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Newborn Fake News Websites Replace Recently Shut Down Ones Within Days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High turnover — when flagged sites quickly reappear under new domains — is a behavioral pattern indicating a coordinated or monetized misinformation strategy (Lead Stories example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cloning/mainstream-site impersonation
rubrics_metrics.description: Spreading disinformation by cloning news sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creating near-identical copies of legitimate news sites (clones) to lend credibility to false stories; referenced as a tactic in 'Part 1: Spreading disinformation by cloning news sites' (Qurium Media Foundation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperpartisan sensationalism for monetization
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Anger is a useful metric' and other evil tips for making money off hyper-partisan content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of emotionally charged, hyperpartisan headlines and content designed to drive clicks and ad revenue is cited as a hallmark of many fake-news operations (Nieman Lab reference; CNBC/Craig Gillin examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal exposure (libel/defamation suits)
rubrics_metrics.description: The most aggressive fake news sites ... are routinely sued by victims of these published reports for libel and defamation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent or notable legal actions against a site for false reporting are an indicator of problematic journalistic practices and may be listed as part of the site's negative profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amplification via social platforms and fringe boards
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories/4chan board posts were quickly picked up and magnified by The Gateway Pundit ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rapid pickup and amplification on social media, message boards, and influencer networks — especially when traceable to fringe sources — is an indicator of disinformation spread dynamics.
